items.content: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies.To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

items.titleZh: 特朗普称美国正式将AI更名为“超级智能”
items.descriptionZh:
在美国总统特朗普于联合国大会周二上午的讲话中，他一边抨击伊朗、“全球主义者”、气候变化和跨性别群体，一边宣称美国“正式”将人工智能（AI）改名为“超级智能”（super intelligence）。原文指出，这一改名并未出现在他几天前发起相关话题时发布的投票选项中。

特朗普给出的理由是：“artificial（人工的）这个词让 intelligence（智能）听起来是假的。”原文作者反问：这真的是让它听起来假的原因吗？并称自己能想到其他理由。此前特朗普曾下令重命名墨西哥湾、苏必利尔湖、肯尼迪中心和德纳里峰等，数字地图也很快为美国用户切换标签。但谈到AI改名时，他说“看看我有没有这个权力。也许有，也许没有，很快见分晓”。

特朗普在讲话中称，美国拒绝任何构建“全球主义计划”来控制人工智能的企图，并宣布此后“正式称为超级智能”，因为“人工”一词让智能显得虚假；它并不假，实际上很了不起，但必须小心。他称，从今往后，美国所有文件——并希望世界各国的文件——都将改用“super”而非“artificial”这一“更准确”的术语，即“super intelligence”（SI）。他反复说这个名称“听起来更好、更准确”，但也承认能否推行要看自己是否有权。

随后，他把“超级智能”与美国政治叙事捆绑：称每项重大新技术都带来挑战，超级智能也不例外；但当年说全球变暖会导致人类12年内灭绝的人——后来因为地球在变冷而非变暖、也没人死，就改称气候变化——如今又在说AI会杀死所有人、机器人会攻击人类，一切都会变成灾难。他还把这些人与“通俄门”“乌克兰门”、气候变化、开放边境等说法归为同一群体，并称“谁赢得AI，现在要说谁赢得SI/超级智能，谁就赢”。他声称美国目前大幅领先中国和其他所有国家，并将保持领先；不会扼杀这个“比工业革命还大、甚至比互联网还大”的增长，同时会通过司法部和其他执法机构密切观察，必要时加以约束，但总体是鼓励而非压制。最后他称美国将在超级智能领域继续安全、负责任地领先，并称美国人不会从边疆退缩，也不会放弃自由。原文以“Developing…”结尾，表明事件仍在发展。

从技术和政策角度看，这篇报道并没有给出任何实际的技术创新、芯片参数或法律文本。原文更强调：特朗普所谓“正式改名”缺乏可验证的官方机制；“superintelligence/超级智能”在AI研究中通常指超越人类智能的假想系统，并非当前AI的简单同义词；而“artificial”在技术语境中意为“人造的”，并非“虚假的”。因此，这一表态更像是政治传播和术语争夺，可能影响美国政府文件、国际AI话语和公众认知，但不会直接改变AI芯片、模型或产业竞争的技术路线。

items.title: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 Advances Agentic, Open Source Robotics Development
items.description: To build and deploy sophisticated robotics applications that can perceive, reason and act in dynamic environments, developers need new physical AI models and tools. items.content: To build and deploy sophisticated robotics applications that can perceive, reason and act in dynamic environments, developers need new physical AI models and tools. The ROS open framework is a project from Open Robotics that helps humans build robots. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 — a collection of GPU-accelerated packages built on ROS, released today at the ROSCon conference in Toronto, Canada — helps humans and AI agents build robots together. The release introduces new agentic workflows and platform support to help developers build, customize and deploy robotics applications faster. ROS provides the open source foundation for much of modern robotics development, giving developers common tools, libraries and standards for building and connecting robot applications. NVIDIA Isaac ROS brings NVIDIA accelerated computing, physical AI models and production-ready libraries to the nearly 1.3 million ROS users, helping developers build high-performance robotics applications using free, familiar, open source tools. Bringing AI Agents Into Robotics Development AI agents are changing how software is built, helping developers automate repetitive tasks, navigate complex codebases and move from ideas to working applications faster. Isaac ROS 5.0 brings these capabilities to robotics development. Isaac ROS 5.0 introduces support for ROS Lyrical and Ubuntu 24.04, giving developers a path to adopt the latest ROS platform while continuing to accelerate demanding robotics workloads with NVIDIA accelerated computing. NVIDIA worked with the Open Source Robotics Alliance to contribute a standard data-handling interface to ROS Lyrical that helps robotics software work efficiently across different computing hardware, including GPUs. Available to the entire ROS community, it gives developers a consistent way to accelerate demanding robotics applications, with CUDA providing a working example for GPU acceleration. New NVIDIA Isaac skills for setup and manipulation provide reusable workflows that developers and AI agents can use to complete robotics development tasks. Agent-ready documentation also makes it easier for AI agents to understand Isaac ROS tools and workflows, turning developer intent into working applications faster. Some skills go beyond assisting with individual coding tasks. A new FoundationStereo fine-tuning skill enables an AI agent to help adapt a stereo perception model to a developer’s cameras, environment and robotics application, so developers can easily achieve more accurate perception for a given sensor configuration. FoundationPose, a foundation model for object pose estimation and tracking, now provides an agent-ready inference library that enables robots to perceive and track the position and orientation of objects up to 5.5x faster. In addition, pick and place — a common workflow that connects detection, depth estimation and pose output — is now available as a standalone, agent-ready skill, providing robot developers more flexibility beyond Isaac ROS. Accelerating the Open Source Robotics Ecosystem The robotics ecosystem is already extending this agentic approach to development workflows. AgenticROS, an open source project sponsored by 3D perception technology company RealSense, connects Isaac ROS with NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints, enabling AI agents to interact with ROS-based robots. RealSense is also optimizing its latest AI-native 3D stereo depth cameras, including RealSense D585 Pro, and an open source software development kit for Isaac ROS and the NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge AI platform, helping developers build perception, navigation and manipulation applications. Intrinsic’s Open Machine Tending Solution is a reference application for computer numerical control machine tending, part of the newly released Intrinsic Core, an open source suite of preconfigured runtime services and capabilities designed to accelerate industrial robotics applications. It includes built-in compatibility with NVIDIA FoundationPose for out-of-the-box object registration, tracking and pose estimation. Using the FoundationPose perception pipeline, the solution enables robots to dynamically detect and handle parts while reducing the need for rigid, costly physical fixtures and specialized systems integration. Intrinsic uses FoundationPose to perform seamless object perception in its Open Machine Tending Solution. Seeed Studio is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS with reBot Arm, combining accelerated perception, spatial understanding and motion planning on NVIDIA Jetson Thor. This integration gives developers a practical platform for building adaptable physical AI applications, from object localization to collision-aware manipulation and autonomous pick and place. Magna is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS as a modular, GPU-accelerated foundation for robotic perception, synchronized data collection and NVIDIA Isaac GR00T model deployment, pairing it with Isaac Sim hardware-in-the-loop testing to bring intelligent automation from research to real-world manufacturing and mobility — faster and with fewer risks. Magna pairs Isaac ROS with Isaac Sim for hardware-in-the-loop testing for faster deployment. Prefix.dev’s Pixi package-management tool makes it easier to create reproducible robot development environments, bringing together ROS with the NVIDIA CUDA platform to help developers more easily set up and share accelerated robotics workflows. As an Isaac ROS Partner, Foxglove helps developers visualize and debug live ROS applications through its web and desktop tools, which are integrated throughout Isaac ROS tutorials and support data such as 3D topics, nvblox meshes and rosbags. Flexiv is integrating Isaac ROS with its Rizon 4 adaptive robot, giving developers access to NVIDIA-accelerated robotics capabilities and a streamlined path from testing applications in NVIDIA Isaac Sim to deploying them on a physical robot. A Flexiv robot developed with Isaac ROS and Isaac Sim deployed as a welding arm in a car factory. Ekumen, a Grid Dynamics Company, is using GPU-accelerated Isaac ROS packages within existing ROS and Nav2 stacks to improve precision docking, 3D obstacle detection, visual localization and real-time motion planning, validating each application in Isaac Sim. Ekumen uses isaac_ros_cumotion on a GPU to map a collision-free path for a warehouse arm in roughly 2 to 5 milliseconds. Ouster integrates its Stereolabs ZED stereo cameras with NVIDIA Isaac ROS to deliver GPU-accelerated perception for robotics applications. The integration simplifies the development of real-time object detection, mapping and navigation while maintaining interoperability with the broader ROS ecosystem. Bringing the Complete Physical AI Stack to the Robot The applications that developers and agents build ultimately need to run on the robot. NVIDIA Jetson is a scalable computing platform for running the physical AI stack at the edge with real-time performance, bringing together ROS, accelerated perception and navigation, AI models and application logic on the robot. Isaac ROS 5.0 supports scalable compute, from entry-level NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano to high-performance Jetson Thor devices, giving developers a path from development to deployment as robotics workloads become increasingly sophisticated. Robotics companies are already using this combination to bring more AI processing directly onto their machines. Mentee Robotics uses NVIDIA Isaac ROS as the perception and AI backbone of its MenteeBot humanoid, enabling the robot to interpret visual information and execute learned behaviors in real time. A shared software foundation across NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms helps Mentee extend its innovations from existing robots to next-generation systems. The MenteeBot humanoid robot uses Isaac ROS to scale its perception capabilities across Jetson hardware platforms. Universal Robots has built NVIDIA Isaac ROS into its AI Accelerator software development kit to help integrators deploy advanced perception and motion capabilities faster, without developing complex robotics software from scratch. Powered by NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, the solution enables robots to adapt to parts that are not precisely positioned, reducing reliance on costly fixtures and making manufacturing cells more flexible. ROBOTIS, which builds the developer-friendly ROS-based TurtleBot3, is integrating Isaac ROS into its AI Worker robot, using GPU-accelerated object perception to enable vision-guided manipulation tasks including picking, placing and alignment. ROBOTIS performs object manipulation tasks using NVIDIA Isaac ROS CuMotion. FieldAI’s robot foundation models, which can run entirely on robots without relying on cloud connectivity, are integrating Isaac ROS on Jetson devices to take greater advantage of GPU acceleration and improve the efficiency of the on-robot AI stack. Noble Machines is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS on Jetson to accelerate the development of general-purpose robots for industrial applications, building on ready-to-use AI and perception capabilities rather than creating them from scratch. By combining an open robotics ecosystem, accelerated computing and new agentic development workflows, Isaac ROS 5.0 helps developers address both sides of the physical AI challenge: building increasingly capable robot applications and efficiently running them in the physical world. Available now, Isaac ROS 5.0 is free and open source. Developers can learn more and get started with NVIDIA Isaac ROS on GitHub.

items.titleZh: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 推动代理式、开源机器人技术发展
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 在加拿大多伦多举行的 ROSCon 大会上发布 Isaac ROS 5.0。其背景是：要构建和部署能在动态环境中感知、推理并行动的复杂机器人应用，开发者需要新的物理 AI 模型和工具。ROS 是 Open Robotics 推出的开源框架，为现代机器人开发提供了通用工具、库和标准，全球已有近 130 万 ROS 用户。NVIDIA Isaac ROS 则是在 ROS 之上构建的一套 GPU 加速软件包，把 NVIDIA 的加速计算、物理 AI 模型和生产级库带给 ROS 社区，使开发者能继续使用免费、熟悉和开源的工具构建高性能机器人应用。Isaac ROS 5.0 的核心目标是让人类和 AI 智能体可以协作开发机器人。

这一版本引入了“智能体化”开发工作流和新的平台支持。AI 智能体正在改变软件开发方式，可自动完成重复任务、理解复杂代码库，并更快把想法变成可运行应用；Isaac ROS 5.0 将这种能力带入机器人开发。它支持 ROS Lyrical 和 Ubuntu 24.04，让开发者能够采用最新 ROS 平台，同时继续用 NVIDIA 加速计算处理高负载机器人工作。NVIDIA 还与 Open Source Robotics Alliance 合作，向 ROS Lyrical 贡献标准数据处理接口，使机器人软件能跨不同计算硬件高效运行，包括 GPU；该接口面向整个 ROS 社区开放，CUDA 则提供了 GPU 加速的可运行示例。新推出的 NVIDIA Isaac skills 覆盖设置和操作等任务，为开发者和 AI 智能体提供可复用工作流；面向智能体的文档也让 AI 更容易理解 Isaac ROS 工具与流程，从而更快把开发者意图转化为应用。一些 skill 不只辅助单个编码任务：新的 FoundationStereo 微调 skill 可让 AI 智能体帮助把立体感知模型适配到开发者使用的相机、环境和机器人应用，以便在特定传感器配置下获得更准确感知。FoundationPose 是用于物体位姿估计和跟踪的基础模型，现在提供面向智能体的推理库，使机器人感知和跟踪物体位置与方向的速度最高提升 5.5 倍。此外，抓取和放置这一连接检测、深度估计与位姿输出的常见工作流，现在也作为独立、面向智能体的 skill 提供，为机器人开发者带来超出 Isaac ROS 的更多灵活性。

机器人生态已在把这种智能体化方法扩展到开发流程中。由 3D 感知公司 RealSense 赞助的开源项目 AgenticROS 将 Isaac ROS 与 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型及 NVIDIA NemoClaw 蓝图连接起来，使 AI 智能体能够与基于 ROS 的机器人交互。RealSense 还在优化其最新 AI 原生 3D 立体深度相机，包括 RealSense D585 Pro，并为 Isaac ROS 和 NVIDIA Jetson Thor 边缘 AI 平台提供开源软件开发套件，帮助开发者构建感知、导航和操作应用。Intrinsic 的 Open Machine Tending Solution 是面向计算机数控机床看护的参考应用，属于新发布的 Intrinsic Core——一套旨在加速工业机器人应用的开源预配置运行时服务与能力。它内置对 NVIDIA FoundationPose 的兼容，可实现开箱即用的物体注册、跟踪和位姿估计；借助 FoundationPose 感知流水线，机器人能动态检测和处理零件，减少对刚性、昂贵物理夹具和专用系统集成的依赖。Seeed Studio 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 与 reBot Arm 结合，在 NVIDIA Jetson Thor 上融合加速感知、空间理解和运动规划，为从物体定位到碰撞感知操作及自主抓取放置提供实用物理 AI 平台。Magna 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 用作模块化、GPU 加速的机器人感知、同步数据采集和 NVIDIA Isaac GR00T 模型部署基础，并与 Isaac Sim 硬件在环测试配合，更快、更低风险地把智能自动化从研究带入真实制造和移动场景。Prefix.dev 的 Pixi 包管理工具可简化可复现机器人开发环境的创建，把 ROS 与 NVIDIA CUDA 平台结合，帮助开发者更轻松设置和分享加速机器人工作流。作为 Isaac ROS 合作伙伴，Foxglove 通过其网页和桌面工具帮助开发者可视化并调试实时 ROS 应用，这些工具已集成到 Isaac ROS 教程中，并支持 3D 话题、nvblox 网格和 rosbag 等数据。Flexiv 正在把 Isaac ROS 集成到其 Rizon 4 自适应机器人中，让开发者获得 NVIDIA 加速机器人能力，并打通从 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 测试应用到物理机器人部署的路径；其机器人已被部署为汽车工厂焊接臂。Ekumen（Grid Dynamics 旗下公司）在现有 ROS 和 Nav2 栈中使用 GPU 加速的 Isaac ROS 包，改进精准对接、3D 障碍物检测、视觉定位和实时运动规划，并在 Isaac Sim 中验证每个应用。Ekumen 使用 GPU 上的 isaac_ros_cumotion 为仓库机械臂规划无碰撞路径，耗时约 2 到 5 毫秒。Ouster 将 Stereolabs ZED 立体相机与 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 集成，为机器人应用提供 GPU 加速感知，简化实时物体检测、建图和导航开发，同时保持与更广泛 ROS 生态的互操作性。

开发者与智能体构建的应用最终需要运行在机器人上。NVIDIA Jetson 是可扩展计算平台，可在边缘以实时性能运行完整物理 AI 栈，把 ROS、加速感知与导航、AI 模型和应用逻辑汇集到机器人端。Isaac ROS 5.0 支持从入门级 NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 到高性能 Jetson Thor 的可扩展计算，为机器人工作负载日益复杂化提供从开发到部署的路径。多家机器人公司已在使用这一组合，把更多 AI 处理直接放到机器上。Mentee Robotics 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 作为其 MenteeBot 人形机器人的感知和 AI 骨干，使机器人能实时解释视觉信息并执行已学习行为；Jetson Orin 和 Jetson Thor 平台共享软件基础，帮助 Mentee 把创新从现有机器人扩展到下一代系统。Universal Robots 已将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 内置到其 AI Accelerator 软件开发套件中，帮助集成商更快部署先进感知和运动能力，而无需从零开发复杂机器人软件；该方案由边缘端 NVIDIA Jetson 驱动，使机器人能适应未精确定位的零件，减少对昂贵夹具的依赖，让制造单元更灵活。ROBOTIS 开发了面向开发者的 ROS 机器人 TurtleBot3，正把 Isaac ROS 集成到其 AI Worker 机器人中，利用 GPU 加速物体感知实现视觉引导的抓取、放置和对齐等操作任务，并使用 NVIDIA Isaac ROS CuMotion 执行物体操作。FieldAI 的机器人基础模型可完全在机器人上运行，不依赖云连接，目前正在 Jetson 设备上集成 Isaac ROS，以更好利用 GPU 加速并提升机器人端 AI 栈效率。Noble Machines 在 Jetson 上使用 NVIDIA Isaac ROS，加速面向工业应用的通用机器人开发，基于现成 AI 和感知能力而非从零构建。通过结合开放机器人生态、加速计算和新的智能体开发工作流，Isaac ROS 5.0 帮助开发者应对物理 AI 的两大挑战：构建能力越来越强的机器人应用，并让它们在物理世界中高效运行。Isaac ROS 5.0 现已发布，免费且开源，开发者可在 GitHub 上了解并开始使用。

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic scramble for smaller data centers as massive gigawatt projects lag
items.description: OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking to secure immediate capacity, through smaller data center deals, to meet current demand, despite spending billions on massive deals elsewhere.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly scrambling to secure smaller AI data center deployments as they race to bring more compute capacity online while gigawatt-scale projects undergo construction. According to a September 18 CNBC report, the two AI giants are exploring agreements for existing facilities with roughly 20-30 MW of capacity, despite already committing tens of billions of dollars to much larger AI infrastructure projects.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleAnthropic has reportedly sounded out potential deals of that size across the UK and Nordic countries, according to CNBC, citing four people familiar with the discussions. OpenAI has also explored smaller deployments in the Nordics, while sources said both companies have discussed similar opportunities in the United States.“We’re building a diversified compute portfolio to meet growing demand for AI around the world,” an OpenAI spokesperson told CNBC. The company added that different workloads require different infrastructure and that it evaluates potential deployments based on performance, reliability, timing, and cost. Anthropic declined to comment.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The smaller facilities would complement the enormous AI campuses both companies are already pursuing. Anthropic, for example, reportedly signed a roughly $45 billion agreement with Nscale for around 460 MW of compute capacity at a West Virginia development. OpenAI, meanwhile, said earlier this year that its Stargate infrastructure commitments had already surpassed the project's original 10 GW target, before announcing another 3 GW in Georgia and 8 GW in Ohio.These projects provide the large clusters of accelerators needed to train increasingly large AI models, in which thousands of GPUs must work together via high-bandwidth interconnects. However, they also take years to develop, requiring land, grid connections, substations, cooling infrastructure, and huge amounts of power before the accelerators can begin operations. You may like Big Tech eyes glacier-strewn Patagonia for building mega AI data centers Data centers forecast to use 20% of US power by 2035 Local opposition blocked $68 billion worth of data center projects in the second quarter of 2026 Meanwhile, both OpenAI and Anthropic need immediate capacity to meet the inference demand for their models. As it turns out, inference can be distributed across multiple smaller clusters, making smaller data centers appropriate for these tasks and increasing the demand for such facilities.Smaller deployments also circumvent some of the issues plaguing large data center buildouts. In the U.S. alone, local opposition blocked 45 data center projects worth $68 billion in the second quarter of 2026 over land usage, noise pollution, and electricity and water consumption. Existing, small facilities do not face the same pressure.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors“Securing a few megawatts at an existing powered site can be more practical than waiting for a much larger block in one location,” Jabez Tan, head of research at Structure Research, told CNBC. “For workloads that can operate across separate sites, a collection of smaller deployments can add up to substantial capacity.”Renting capacity is already standard practice for AI companies, as AI labs lease capacity from hyperscalers, dedicated data center operators, and rapidly expanding GPU-focused neoclouds. This allows them to spread workloads across multiple providers. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: OpenAI和Anthropic争相寻求小型数据中心，千兆瓦级大项目滞后
items.descriptionZh:
Anthropic 和 OpenAI 据 CNBC 9月18日报道，正争相锁定规模更小的 AI 数据中心部署，以便在吉瓦级大型项目仍在建设时尽快增加算力。知情人士称，两家公司正在探索容量约 20-30 兆瓦的现有设施协议，尽管它们已向更大规模 AI 基础设施投入数十亿美元。Anthropic 已在英国和北欧国家试探此类交易，OpenAI 也在北欧寻找小型部署，并据称在美国讨论类似机会。OpenAI 发言人表示，公司正构建多元化算力组合以满足全球 AI 需求，不同工作负载需要不同基础设施，并会基于性能、可靠性、时间安排和成本评估部署；Anthropic 拒绝置评。

这些较小设施将补充两家公司已在推进的大型 AI 园区。Anthropic 据报道与 Nscale 签署约 450 亿美元协议，在西弗吉尼亚开发约 460 兆瓦算力。OpenAI 今年早些时候称，其 Stargate 基础设施承诺已超过项目最初 10 吉瓦目标，随后又宣布在佐治亚州新增 3 吉瓦、在俄亥俄州新增 8 吉瓦。此类大型项目能提供训练日益庞大 AI 模型所需的大型加速器集群，其中数千块 GPU 必须通过高带宽互连协同工作。但它们开发周期长达数年，需要土地、电网连接、变电站、冷却基础设施和大量电力，之后加速器才能开始运行。

与此同时，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 需要即时容量来满足其模型的推理需求。核心技术逻辑在于：训练通常依赖集中式超大集群，而推理可以分布在多个较小集群上，因此 20-30 兆瓦级的小型数据中心适合承担推理任务，并推高了对这类设施的需求。这种部署策略的创新点在于“化整为零”：利用现有已供电站点快速获得算力，避免等待大型项目漫长的审批、建设和并网过程。小型部署还能绕开大型数据中心面临的部分阻力。仅在美国，2026 年第二季度就有 45 个数据中心项目、价值 680 亿美元因土地使用、噪音污染以及电力和水消耗引发的当地反对而被阻止；现有小型设施面临的压力则小得多。

Structure Research 研究主管 Jabez Tan 对 CNBC 表示，在现有已供电站点获得几兆瓦容量，可能比等待某一地点放出更大容量块更实际；对于可跨不同站点运行的工作负载，多个小型部署加起来也能形成可观容量。事实上，租赁容量已是 AI 公司的标准做法，AI 实验室从超大规模云厂商、专用数据中心运营商以及快速扩张的 GPU 型 neoclouds 租用算力，从而将工作负载分散到多个供应商。整体来看，这一动向反映出 AI 行业的算力瓶颈正从训练扩展到推理，部署灵活性、上市时间和分布式推理能力正成为关键竞争要素；大型园区继续为前沿模型训练提供基础，而小型设施则更快支撑全球推理服务。

items.titleZh: 并发HBM与主机内存访问提升LLM推理吞吐量（佐治亚理工学院、英伟达、斯坦福大学）
items.descriptionZh:
佐治亚理工学院、NVIDIA Research 与斯坦福大学的研究人员联合发表了题为《BOOST: Concurrent Access to Host Memory and HBM to Accelerate LLM Inference》的技术论文。Semiconductor Engineering 报道称，BOOST 是首个能够并发且按比例访问 GPU 两个内存层级的运行时系统，可把主机内存与 HBM 的带宽叠加起来，用于加速大语言模型（LLM）推理。

背景上，LLM 推理，特别是自回归解码阶段，是典型的内存带宽受限负载：每生成一个 token，都要读取全部或大部分模型权重以及不断增长的 KV cache。HBM 带宽高，但容量有限、成本高；主机 DRAM/LPDDR 容量大、成本低，但传统上只能作为慢速后备，通过 PCIe/NVLink 进行 offload 或统一内存页迁移，访问往往与 HBM 串行，无法同时供数。因此，现有系统要么受 HBM 容量限制，要么因主机内存延迟和带宽瓶颈而降低吞吐。

BOOST 的创新在于把主机内存从“容量扩展”变成“带宽扩展”。它不是简单地把数据换出到 CPU 内存，而是让 GPU 同时向 HBM 和主机内存发起访问，并按两者的可用带宽、延迟和访问特征动态分配请求比例。例如，高带宽 HBM 承担大部分流量，较低带宽的主机内存承担较小比例，使两个层级并行工作、尽可能同时饱和，从而获得高于单独 HBM 的有效带宽。摘要强调这是首个提供“并发且按比例”访问两个 GPU 内存层级的运行时系统。结合作者背景与平台趋势，该工作很可能面向 NVIDIA Grace Hopper 等通过 NVLink-C2C 高速互连 HBM 与 LPDDR 主机内存的超级芯片，利用主机内存的额外带宽缓解 HBM 瓶颈。

性能上，报道标题直接指出，并发访问 HBM 和主机内存可提升 LLM 推理吞吐量。其收益主要来自解码阶段：吞吐受内存带宽限制，组合带宽越高，每秒生成的 token 越多。与仅用 HBM 相比，BOOST 可额外利用主机内存带宽；与完全 offload 到主机内存相比，它避免所有数据都走低速链路，因此吞吐损失小得多。摘要节选未给出具体加速比、带宽利用率和基准模型数据，但“提取组合带宽”表明其目标是让两类内存并行供数，而非串行回退。

应用场景包括超大模型单机推理、长上下文和 KV cache 密集型服务、大 batch 推理、多租户 LLM 服务，以及 Grace Hopper/Blackwell 等统一内存超级芯片平台。技术影响上，BOOST 挑战了“主机内存只是慢速后备”的传统观念，提出用运行时调度把 HBM 与主机内存聚合成更高有效带宽，有助于降低对昂贵 HBM 容量的依赖、提升每美元吞吐，并可能影响未来 GPU 内存管理、编译器调度以及 CXL/异构内存系统设计。

items.titleZh: Can Agents Design  Better Chips When Operating At A Higher Level Of Abstraction Using HLS (UCLA)
items.descriptionZh:
加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）的研究团队发表了一篇题为《Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?》的技术论文，探讨大语言模型（LLM）智能体在芯片设计中应采用何种抽象层次。当前，LLM智能体已被越来越多地用于芯片设计，但大多数方案直接工作在寄存器传输级（RTL），即让模型生成Verilog/VHDL等底层硬件描述。RTL设计需要精确处理时钟、位宽、握手协议、流水线和微架构细节，设计空间庞大且容易出错，LLM智能体难以在架构层面有效探索。UCLA团队因此提出：如果让智能体在更高抽象层——高层次综合（HLS）——上工作，即生成C/C++/SystemC等高层代码，再由HLS工具自动综合为RTL，是否能让智能体设计出更好的芯片？

论文的核心方法是系统比较“直接RTL生成”与“基于HLS的智能体设计流程”。在HLS流程中，LLM智能体根据自然语言规格或算法描述生成可综合的高层代码，并可插入流水线、循环展开、数据流等综合指令；HLS工具将其转换为RTL，同时给出时序、资源和功耗报告。智能体利用仿真、综合和PPA反馈进行多轮迭代，修正功能并优化设计。其创新点在于把抽象层次作为核心变量，评估HLS对LLM智能体设计能力的影响，并构建可迭代的代理框架，使LLM从底层时序细节中解放出来，更专注于算法、并行度和架构权衡。

对比实验通常考察功能正确率、综合成功率、迭代次数、代码复杂度以及最终PPA（性能、功耗、面积）。论文结果表明，HLS抽象能降低LLM生成代码的难度，使其借助HLS工具的自动化优化获得更好的设计效率和正确性，尤其适合较复杂或算法密集型设计；但HLS也引入工具约束、pragma调优和验证复杂性，最终质量仍取决于高层描述和综合指令。因此，更高抽象并非简单替代RTL，而是改变智能体的设计空间和优化目标。

该研究对ASIC/FPGA加速器、边缘AI芯片、领域专用架构和快速原型设计具有启发意义：未来LLM芯片设计可能采用多层代理流程，高层代理负责算法与架构，底层代理负责RTL与物理实现，并与HLS、逻辑综合和验证工具闭环。其影响在于推动芯片设计自动化和设计空间探索，但验证可信度、PPA可预测性和工具兼容性仍是待解决问题。UCLA的工作表明，HLS可能是释放LLM智能体芯片设计能力的重要方向。

history.content: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies.To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

history.titleZh: 特朗普称美国正式将AI更名为“超级智能”
history.descriptionZh:
在美国总统特朗普于联合国大会周二上午的讲话中，他一边抨击伊朗、“全球主义者”、气候变化和跨性别群体，一边宣称美国“正式”将人工智能（AI）改名为“超级智能”（super intelligence）。原文指出，这一改名并未出现在他几天前发起相关话题时发布的投票选项中。

特朗普给出的理由是：“artificial（人工的）这个词让 intelligence（智能）听起来是假的。”原文作者反问：这真的是让它听起来假的原因吗？并称自己能想到其他理由。此前特朗普曾下令重命名墨西哥湾、苏必利尔湖、肯尼迪中心和德纳里峰等，数字地图也很快为美国用户切换标签。但谈到AI改名时，他说“看看我有没有这个权力。也许有，也许没有，很快见分晓”。

特朗普在讲话中称，美国拒绝任何构建“全球主义计划”来控制人工智能的企图，并宣布此后“正式称为超级智能”，因为“人工”一词让智能显得虚假；它并不假，实际上很了不起，但必须小心。他称，从今往后，美国所有文件——并希望世界各国的文件——都将改用“super”而非“artificial”这一“更准确”的术语，即“super intelligence”（SI）。他反复说这个名称“听起来更好、更准确”，但也承认能否推行要看自己是否有权。

随后，他把“超级智能”与美国政治叙事捆绑：称每项重大新技术都带来挑战，超级智能也不例外；但当年说全球变暖会导致人类12年内灭绝的人——后来因为地球在变冷而非变暖、也没人死，就改称气候变化——如今又在说AI会杀死所有人、机器人会攻击人类，一切都会变成灾难。他还把这些人与“通俄门”“乌克兰门”、气候变化、开放边境等说法归为同一群体，并称“谁赢得AI，现在要说谁赢得SI/超级智能，谁就赢”。他声称美国目前大幅领先中国和其他所有国家，并将保持领先；不会扼杀这个“比工业革命还大、甚至比互联网还大”的增长，同时会通过司法部和其他执法机构密切观察，必要时加以约束，但总体是鼓励而非压制。最后他称美国将在超级智能领域继续安全、负责任地领先，并称美国人不会从边疆退缩，也不会放弃自由。原文以“Developing…”结尾，表明事件仍在发展。

从技术和政策角度看，这篇报道并没有给出任何实际的技术创新、芯片参数或法律文本。原文更强调：特朗普所谓“正式改名”缺乏可验证的官方机制；“superintelligence/超级智能”在AI研究中通常指超越人类智能的假想系统，并非当前AI的简单同义词；而“artificial”在技术语境中意为“人造的”，并非“虚假的”。因此，这一表态更像是政治传播和术语争夺，可能影响美国政府文件、国际AI话语和公众认知，但不会直接改变AI芯片、模型或产业竞争的技术路线。

history.title: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 Advances Agentic, Open Source Robotics Development
history.description: To build and deploy sophisticated robotics applications that can perceive, reason and act in dynamic environments, developers need new physical AI models and tools. history.content: To build and deploy sophisticated robotics applications that can perceive, reason and act in dynamic environments, developers need new physical AI models and tools. The ROS open framework is a project from Open Robotics that helps humans build robots. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 — a collection of GPU-accelerated packages built on ROS, released today at the ROSCon conference in Toronto, Canada — helps humans and AI agents build robots together. The release introduces new agentic workflows and platform support to help developers build, customize and deploy robotics applications faster. ROS provides the open source foundation for much of modern robotics development, giving developers common tools, libraries and standards for building and connecting robot applications. NVIDIA Isaac ROS brings NVIDIA accelerated computing, physical AI models and production-ready libraries to the nearly 1.3 million ROS users, helping developers build high-performance robotics applications using free, familiar, open source tools. Bringing AI Agents Into Robotics Development AI agents are changing how software is built, helping developers automate repetitive tasks, navigate complex codebases and move from ideas to working applications faster. Isaac ROS 5.0 brings these capabilities to robotics development. Isaac ROS 5.0 introduces support for ROS Lyrical and Ubuntu 24.04, giving developers a path to adopt the latest ROS platform while continuing to accelerate demanding robotics workloads with NVIDIA accelerated computing. NVIDIA worked with the Open Source Robotics Alliance to contribute a standard data-handling interface to ROS Lyrical that helps robotics software work efficiently across different computing hardware, including GPUs. Available to the entire ROS community, it gives developers a consistent way to accelerate demanding robotics applications, with CUDA providing a working example for GPU acceleration. New NVIDIA Isaac skills for setup and manipulation provide reusable workflows that developers and AI agents can use to complete robotics development tasks. Agent-ready documentation also makes it easier for AI agents to understand Isaac ROS tools and workflows, turning developer intent into working applications faster. Some skills go beyond assisting with individual coding tasks. A new FoundationStereo fine-tuning skill enables an AI agent to help adapt a stereo perception model to a developer’s cameras, environment and robotics application, so developers can easily achieve more accurate perception for a given sensor configuration. FoundationPose, a foundation model for object pose estimation and tracking, now provides an agent-ready inference library that enables robots to perceive and track the position and orientation of objects up to 5.5x faster. In addition, pick and place — a common workflow that connects detection, depth estimation and pose output — is now available as a standalone, agent-ready skill, providing robot developers more flexibility beyond Isaac ROS. Accelerating the Open Source Robotics Ecosystem The robotics ecosystem is already extending this agentic approach to development workflows. AgenticROS, an open source project sponsored by 3D perception technology company RealSense, connects Isaac ROS with NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints, enabling AI agents to interact with ROS-based robots. RealSense is also optimizing its latest AI-native 3D stereo depth cameras, including RealSense D585 Pro, and an open source software development kit for Isaac ROS and the NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge AI platform, helping developers build perception, navigation and manipulation applications. Intrinsic’s Open Machine Tending Solution is a reference application for computer numerical control machine tending, part of the newly released Intrinsic Core, an open source suite of preconfigured runtime services and capabilities designed to accelerate industrial robotics applications. It includes built-in compatibility with NVIDIA FoundationPose for out-of-the-box object registration, tracking and pose estimation. Using the FoundationPose perception pipeline, the solution enables robots to dynamically detect and handle parts while reducing the need for rigid, costly physical fixtures and specialized systems integration. Intrinsic uses FoundationPose to perform seamless object perception in its Open Machine Tending Solution. Seeed Studio is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS with reBot Arm, combining accelerated perception, spatial understanding and motion planning on NVIDIA Jetson Thor. This integration gives developers a practical platform for building adaptable physical AI applications, from object localization to collision-aware manipulation and autonomous pick and place. Magna is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS as a modular, GPU-accelerated foundation for robotic perception, synchronized data collection and NVIDIA Isaac GR00T model deployment, pairing it with Isaac Sim hardware-in-the-loop testing to bring intelligent automation from research to real-world manufacturing and mobility — faster and with fewer risks. Magna pairs Isaac ROS with Isaac Sim for hardware-in-the-loop testing for faster deployment. Prefix.dev’s Pixi package-management tool makes it easier to create reproducible robot development environments, bringing together ROS with the NVIDIA CUDA platform to help developers more easily set up and share accelerated robotics workflows. As an Isaac ROS Partner, Foxglove helps developers visualize and debug live ROS applications through its web and desktop tools, which are integrated throughout Isaac ROS tutorials and support data such as 3D topics, nvblox meshes and rosbags. Flexiv is integrating Isaac ROS with its Rizon 4 adaptive robot, giving developers access to NVIDIA-accelerated robotics capabilities and a streamlined path from testing applications in NVIDIA Isaac Sim to deploying them on a physical robot. A Flexiv robot developed with Isaac ROS and Isaac Sim deployed as a welding arm in a car factory. Ekumen, a Grid Dynamics Company, is using GPU-accelerated Isaac ROS packages within existing ROS and Nav2 stacks to improve precision docking, 3D obstacle detection, visual localization and real-time motion planning, validating each application in Isaac Sim. Ekumen uses isaac_ros_cumotion on a GPU to map a collision-free path for a warehouse arm in roughly 2 to 5 milliseconds. Ouster integrates its Stereolabs ZED stereo cameras with NVIDIA Isaac ROS to deliver GPU-accelerated perception for robotics applications. The integration simplifies the development of real-time object detection, mapping and navigation while maintaining interoperability with the broader ROS ecosystem. Bringing the Complete Physical AI Stack to the Robot The applications that developers and agents build ultimately need to run on the robot. NVIDIA Jetson is a scalable computing platform for running the physical AI stack at the edge with real-time performance, bringing together ROS, accelerated perception and navigation, AI models and application logic on the robot. Isaac ROS 5.0 supports scalable compute, from entry-level NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano to high-performance Jetson Thor devices, giving developers a path from development to deployment as robotics workloads become increasingly sophisticated. Robotics companies are already using this combination to bring more AI processing directly onto their machines. Mentee Robotics uses NVIDIA Isaac ROS as the perception and AI backbone of its MenteeBot humanoid, enabling the robot to interpret visual information and execute learned behaviors in real time. A shared software foundation across NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms helps Mentee extend its innovations from existing robots to next-generation systems. The MenteeBot humanoid robot uses Isaac ROS to scale its perception capabilities across Jetson hardware platforms. Universal Robots has built NVIDIA Isaac ROS into its AI Accelerator software development kit to help integrators deploy advanced perception and motion capabilities faster, without developing complex robotics software from scratch. Powered by NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, the solution enables robots to adapt to parts that are not precisely positioned, reducing reliance on costly fixtures and making manufacturing cells more flexible. ROBOTIS, which builds the developer-friendly ROS-based TurtleBot3, is integrating Isaac ROS into its AI Worker robot, using GPU-accelerated object perception to enable vision-guided manipulation tasks including picking, placing and alignment. ROBOTIS performs object manipulation tasks using NVIDIA Isaac ROS CuMotion. FieldAI’s robot foundation models, which can run entirely on robots without relying on cloud connectivity, are integrating Isaac ROS on Jetson devices to take greater advantage of GPU acceleration and improve the efficiency of the on-robot AI stack. Noble Machines is using NVIDIA Isaac ROS on Jetson to accelerate the development of general-purpose robots for industrial applications, building on ready-to-use AI and perception capabilities rather than creating them from scratch. By combining an open robotics ecosystem, accelerated computing and new agentic development workflows, Isaac ROS 5.0 helps developers address both sides of the physical AI challenge: building increasingly capable robot applications and efficiently running them in the physical world. Available now, Isaac ROS 5.0 is free and open source. Developers can learn more and get started with NVIDIA Isaac ROS on GitHub.
history.author: Katie Washabaugh
history.titleZh: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 推动代理式、开源机器人技术发展
history.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 在加拿大多伦多举行的 ROSCon 大会上发布 Isaac ROS 5.0。其背景是：要构建和部署能在动态环境中感知、推理并行动的复杂机器人应用，开发者需要新的物理 AI 模型和工具。ROS 是 Open Robotics 推出的开源框架，为现代机器人开发提供了通用工具、库和标准，全球已有近 130 万 ROS 用户。NVIDIA Isaac ROS 则是在 ROS 之上构建的一套 GPU 加速软件包，把 NVIDIA 的加速计算、物理 AI 模型和生产级库带给 ROS 社区，使开发者能继续使用免费、熟悉和开源的工具构建高性能机器人应用。Isaac ROS 5.0 的核心目标是让人类和 AI 智能体可以协作开发机器人。

这一版本引入了“智能体化”开发工作流和新的平台支持。AI 智能体正在改变软件开发方式，可自动完成重复任务、理解复杂代码库，并更快把想法变成可运行应用；Isaac ROS 5.0 将这种能力带入机器人开发。它支持 ROS Lyrical 和 Ubuntu 24.04，让开发者能够采用最新 ROS 平台，同时继续用 NVIDIA 加速计算处理高负载机器人工作。NVIDIA 还与 Open Source Robotics Alliance 合作，向 ROS Lyrical 贡献标准数据处理接口，使机器人软件能跨不同计算硬件高效运行，包括 GPU；该接口面向整个 ROS 社区开放，CUDA 则提供了 GPU 加速的可运行示例。新推出的 NVIDIA Isaac skills 覆盖设置和操作等任务，为开发者和 AI 智能体提供可复用工作流；面向智能体的文档也让 AI 更容易理解 Isaac ROS 工具与流程，从而更快把开发者意图转化为应用。一些 skill 不只辅助单个编码任务：新的 FoundationStereo 微调 skill 可让 AI 智能体帮助把立体感知模型适配到开发者使用的相机、环境和机器人应用，以便在特定传感器配置下获得更准确感知。FoundationPose 是用于物体位姿估计和跟踪的基础模型，现在提供面向智能体的推理库，使机器人感知和跟踪物体位置与方向的速度最高提升 5.5 倍。此外，抓取和放置这一连接检测、深度估计与位姿输出的常见工作流，现在也作为独立、面向智能体的 skill 提供，为机器人开发者带来超出 Isaac ROS 的更多灵活性。

机器人生态已在把这种智能体化方法扩展到开发流程中。由 3D 感知公司 RealSense 赞助的开源项目 AgenticROS 将 Isaac ROS 与 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型及 NVIDIA NemoClaw 蓝图连接起来，使 AI 智能体能够与基于 ROS 的机器人交互。RealSense 还在优化其最新 AI 原生 3D 立体深度相机，包括 RealSense D585 Pro，并为 Isaac ROS 和 NVIDIA Jetson Thor 边缘 AI 平台提供开源软件开发套件，帮助开发者构建感知、导航和操作应用。Intrinsic 的 Open Machine Tending Solution 是面向计算机数控机床看护的参考应用，属于新发布的 Intrinsic Core——一套旨在加速工业机器人应用的开源预配置运行时服务与能力。它内置对 NVIDIA FoundationPose 的兼容，可实现开箱即用的物体注册、跟踪和位姿估计；借助 FoundationPose 感知流水线，机器人能动态检测和处理零件，减少对刚性、昂贵物理夹具和专用系统集成的依赖。Seeed Studio 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 与 reBot Arm 结合，在 NVIDIA Jetson Thor 上融合加速感知、空间理解和运动规划，为从物体定位到碰撞感知操作及自主抓取放置提供实用物理 AI 平台。Magna 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 用作模块化、GPU 加速的机器人感知、同步数据采集和 NVIDIA Isaac GR00T 模型部署基础，并与 Isaac Sim 硬件在环测试配合，更快、更低风险地把智能自动化从研究带入真实制造和移动场景。Prefix.dev 的 Pixi 包管理工具可简化可复现机器人开发环境的创建，把 ROS 与 NVIDIA CUDA 平台结合，帮助开发者更轻松设置和分享加速机器人工作流。作为 Isaac ROS 合作伙伴，Foxglove 通过其网页和桌面工具帮助开发者可视化并调试实时 ROS 应用，这些工具已集成到 Isaac ROS 教程中，并支持 3D 话题、nvblox 网格和 rosbag 等数据。Flexiv 正在把 Isaac ROS 集成到其 Rizon 4 自适应机器人中，让开发者获得 NVIDIA 加速机器人能力，并打通从 NVIDIA Isaac Sim 测试应用到物理机器人部署的路径；其机器人已被部署为汽车工厂焊接臂。Ekumen（Grid Dynamics 旗下公司）在现有 ROS 和 Nav2 栈中使用 GPU 加速的 Isaac ROS 包，改进精准对接、3D 障碍物检测、视觉定位和实时运动规划，并在 Isaac Sim 中验证每个应用。Ekumen 使用 GPU 上的 isaac_ros_cumotion 为仓库机械臂规划无碰撞路径，耗时约 2 到 5 毫秒。Ouster 将 Stereolabs ZED 立体相机与 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 集成，为机器人应用提供 GPU 加速感知，简化实时物体检测、建图和导航开发，同时保持与更广泛 ROS 生态的互操作性。

开发者与智能体构建的应用最终需要运行在机器人上。NVIDIA Jetson 是可扩展计算平台，可在边缘以实时性能运行完整物理 AI 栈，把 ROS、加速感知与导航、AI 模型和应用逻辑汇集到机器人端。Isaac ROS 5.0 支持从入门级 NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 到高性能 Jetson Thor 的可扩展计算，为机器人工作负载日益复杂化提供从开发到部署的路径。多家机器人公司已在使用这一组合，把更多 AI 处理直接放到机器上。Mentee Robotics 将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 作为其 MenteeBot 人形机器人的感知和 AI 骨干，使机器人能实时解释视觉信息并执行已学习行为；Jetson Orin 和 Jetson Thor 平台共享软件基础，帮助 Mentee 把创新从现有机器人扩展到下一代系统。Universal Robots 已将 NVIDIA Isaac ROS 内置到其 AI Accelerator 软件开发套件中，帮助集成商更快部署先进感知和运动能力，而无需从零开发复杂机器人软件；该方案由边缘端 NVIDIA Jetson 驱动，使机器人能适应未精确定位的零件，减少对昂贵夹具的依赖，让制造单元更灵活。ROBOTIS 开发了面向开发者的 ROS 机器人 TurtleBot3，正把 Isaac ROS 集成到其 AI Worker 机器人中，利用 GPU 加速物体感知实现视觉引导的抓取、放置和对齐等操作任务，并使用 NVIDIA Isaac ROS CuMotion 执行物体操作。FieldAI 的机器人基础模型可完全在机器人上运行，不依赖云连接，目前正在 Jetson 设备上集成 Isaac ROS，以更好利用 GPU 加速并提升机器人端 AI 栈效率。Noble Machines 在 Jetson 上使用 NVIDIA Isaac ROS，加速面向工业应用的通用机器人开发，基于现成 AI 和感知能力而非从零构建。通过结合开放机器人生态、加速计算和新的智能体开发工作流，Isaac ROS 5.0 帮助开发者应对物理 AI 的两大挑战：构建能力越来越强的机器人应用，并让它们在物理世界中高效运行。Isaac ROS 5.0 现已发布，免费且开源，开发者可在 GitHub 上了解并开始使用。

history.title: OpenAI and Anthropic scramble for smaller data centers as massive gigawatt projects lag
history.description: OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking to secure immediate capacity, through smaller data center deals, to meet current demand, despite spending billions on massive deals elsewhere.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly scrambling to secure smaller AI data center deployments as they race to bring more compute capacity online while gigawatt-scale projects undergo construction. According to a September 18 CNBC report, the two AI giants are exploring agreements for existing facilities with roughly 20-30 MW of capacity, despite already committing tens of billions of dollars to much larger AI infrastructure projects.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleAnthropic has reportedly sounded out potential deals of that size across the UK and Nordic countries, according to CNBC, citing four people familiar with the discussions. OpenAI has also explored smaller deployments in the Nordics, while sources said both companies have discussed similar opportunities in the United States.“We’re building a diversified compute portfolio to meet growing demand for AI around the world,” an OpenAI spokesperson told CNBC. The company added that different workloads require different infrastructure and that it evaluates potential deployments based on performance, reliability, timing, and cost. Anthropic declined to comment.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The smaller facilities would complement the enormous AI campuses both companies are already pursuing. Anthropic, for example, reportedly signed a roughly $45 billion agreement with Nscale for around 460 MW of compute capacity at a West Virginia development. OpenAI, meanwhile, said earlier this year that its Stargate infrastructure commitments had already surpassed the project's original 10 GW target, before announcing another 3 GW in Georgia and 8 GW in Ohio.These projects provide the large clusters of accelerators needed to train increasingly large AI models, in which thousands of GPUs must work together via high-bandwidth interconnects. However, they also take years to develop, requiring land, grid connections, substations, cooling infrastructure, and huge amounts of power before the accelerators can begin operations. You may like Big Tech eyes glacier-strewn Patagonia for building mega AI data centers Data centers forecast to use 20% of US power by 2035 Local opposition blocked $68 billion worth of data center projects in the second quarter of 2026 Meanwhile, both OpenAI and Anthropic need immediate capacity to meet the inference demand for their models. As it turns out, inference can be distributed across multiple smaller clusters, making smaller data centers appropriate for these tasks and increasing the demand for such facilities.Smaller deployments also circumvent some of the issues plaguing large data center buildouts. In the U.S. alone, local opposition blocked 45 data center projects worth $68 billion in the second quarter of 2026 over land usage, noise pollution, and electricity and water consumption. Existing, small facilities do not face the same pressure.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors“Securing a few megawatts at an existing powered site can be more practical than waiting for a much larger block in one location,” Jabez Tan, head of research at Structure Research, told CNBC. “For workloads that can operate across separate sites, a collection of smaller deployments can add up to substantial capacity.”Renting capacity is already standard practice for AI companies, as AI labs lease capacity from hyperscalers, dedicated data center operators, and rapidly expanding GPU-focused neoclouds. history.titleZh: OpenAI和Anthropic争相寻求小型数据中心，千兆瓦级大项目滞后
history.descriptionZh:
Anthropic 和 OpenAI 据 CNBC 9月18日报道，正争相锁定规模更小的 AI 数据中心部署，以便在吉瓦级大型项目仍在建设时尽快增加算力。知情人士称，两家公司正在探索容量约 20-30 兆瓦的现有设施协议，尽管它们已向更大规模 AI 基础设施投入数十亿美元。Anthropic 已在英国和北欧国家试探此类交易，OpenAI 也在北欧寻找小型部署，并据称在美国讨论类似机会。OpenAI 发言人表示，公司正构建多元化算力组合以满足全球 AI 需求，不同工作负载需要不同基础设施，并会基于性能、可靠性、时间安排和成本评估部署；Anthropic 拒绝置评。

这些较小设施将补充两家公司已在推进的大型 AI 园区。Anthropic 据报道与 Nscale 签署约 450 亿美元协议，在西弗吉尼亚开发约 460 兆瓦算力。OpenAI 今年早些时候称，其 Stargate 基础设施承诺已超过项目最初 10 吉瓦目标，随后又宣布在佐治亚州新增 3 吉瓦、在俄亥俄州新增 8 吉瓦。此类大型项目能提供训练日益庞大 AI 模型所需的大型加速器集群，其中数千块 GPU 必须通过高带宽互连协同工作。但它们开发周期长达数年，需要土地、电网连接、变电站、冷却基础设施和大量电力，之后加速器才能开始运行。

与此同时，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 需要即时容量来满足其模型的推理需求。核心技术逻辑在于：训练通常依赖集中式超大集群，而推理可以分布在多个较小集群上，因此 20-30 兆瓦级的小型数据中心适合承担推理任务，并推高了对这类设施的需求。这种部署策略的创新点在于“化整为零”：利用现有已供电站点快速获得算力，避免等待大型项目漫长的审批、建设和并网过程。小型部署还能绕开大型数据中心面临的部分阻力。仅在美国，2026 年第二季度就有 45 个数据中心项目、价值 680 亿美元因土地使用、噪音污染以及电力和水消耗引发的当地反对而被阻止；现有小型设施面临的压力则小得多。

Structure Research 研究主管 Jabez Tan 对 CNBC 表示，在现有已供电站点获得几兆瓦容量，可能比等待某一地点放出更大容量块更实际；对于可跨不同站点运行的工作负载，多个小型部署加起来也能形成可观容量。事实上，租赁容量已是 AI 公司的标准做法，AI 实验室从超大规模云厂商、专用数据中心运营商以及快速扩张的 GPU 型 neoclouds 租用算力，从而将工作负载分散到多个供应商。整体来看，这一动向反映出 AI 行业的算力瓶颈正从训练扩展到推理，部署灵活性、上市时间和分布式推理能力正成为关键竞争要素；大型园区继续为前沿模型训练提供基础，而小型设施则更快支撑全球推理服务。

history.titleZh: 并发HBM与主机内存访问提升LLM推理吞吐量（佐治亚理工学院、英伟达、斯坦福大学）

佐治亚理工学院、NVIDIA Research 与斯坦福大学的研究人员联合发表了题为《BOOST: Concurrent Access to Host Memory and HBM to Accelerate LLM Inference》的技术论文。Semiconductor Engineering 报道称，BOOST 是首个能够并发且按比例访问 GPU 两个内存层级的运行时系统，可把主机内存与 HBM 的带宽叠加起来，用于加速大语言模型（LLM）推理。

背景上，LLM 推理，特别是自回归解码阶段，是典型的内存带宽受限负载：每生成一个 token，都要读取全部或大部分模型权重以及不断增长的 KV cache。HBM 带宽高，但容量有限、成本高；主机 DRAM/LPDDR 容量大、成本低，但传统上只能作为慢速后备，通过 PCIe/NVLink 进行 offload 或统一内存页迁移，访问往往与 HBM 串行，无法同时供数。因此，现有系统要么受 HBM 容量限制，要么因主机内存延迟和带宽瓶颈而降低吞吐。

BOOST 的创新在于把主机内存从“容量扩展”变成“带宽扩展”。它不是简单地把数据换出到 CPU 内存，而是让 GPU 同时向 HBM 和主机内存发起访问，并按两者的可用带宽、延迟和访问特征动态分配请求比例。例如，高带宽 HBM 承担大部分流量，较低带宽的主机内存承担较小比例，使两个层级并行工作、尽可能同时饱和，从而获得高于单独 HBM 的有效带宽。摘要强调这是首个提供“并发且按比例”访问两个 GPU 内存层级的运行时系统。结合作者背景与平台趋势，该工作很可能面向 NVIDIA Grace Hopper 等通过 NVLink-C2C 高速互连 HBM 与 LPDDR 主机内存的超级芯片，利用主机内存的额外带宽缓解 HBM 瓶颈。

性能上，报道标题直接指出，并发访问 HBM 和主机内存可提升 LLM 推理吞吐量。其收益主要来自解码阶段：吞吐受内存带宽限制，组合带宽越高，每秒生成的 token 越多。与仅用 HBM 相比，BOOST 可额外利用主机内存带宽；与完全 offload 到主机内存相比，它避免所有数据都走低速链路，因此吞吐损失小得多。摘要节选未给出具体加速比、带宽利用率和基准模型数据，但“提取组合带宽”表明其目标是让两类内存并行供数，而非串行回退。

应用场景包括超大模型单机推理、长上下文和 KV cache 密集型服务、大 batch 推理、多租户 LLM 服务，以及 Grace Hopper/Blackwell 等统一内存超级芯片平台。技术影响上，BOOST 挑战了“主机内存只是慢速后备”的传统观念，提出用运行时调度把 HBM 与主机内存聚合成更高有效带宽，有助于降低对昂贵 HBM 容量的依赖、提升每美元吞吐，并可能影响未来 GPU 内存管理、编译器调度以及 CXL/异构内存系统设计。

history.titleZh: Can Agents Design  Better Chips When Operating At A Higher Level Of Abstraction Using HLS (UCLA)
history.descriptionZh:
加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）的研究团队发表了一篇题为《Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?》的技术论文，探讨大语言模型（LLM）智能体在芯片设计中应采用何种抽象层次。当前，LLM智能体已被越来越多地用于芯片设计，但大多数方案直接工作在寄存器传输级（RTL），即让模型生成Verilog/VHDL等底层硬件描述。RTL设计需要精确处理时钟、位宽、握手协议、流水线和微架构细节，设计空间庞大且容易出错，LLM智能体难以在架构层面有效探索。UCLA团队因此提出：如果让智能体在更高抽象层——高层次综合（HLS）——上工作，即生成C/C++/SystemC等高层代码，再由HLS工具自动综合为RTL，是否能让智能体设计出更好的芯片？

论文的核心方法是系统比较“直接RTL生成”与“基于HLS的智能体设计流程”。在HLS流程中，LLM智能体根据自然语言规格或算法描述生成可综合的高层代码，并可插入流水线、循环展开、数据流等综合指令；HLS工具将其转换为RTL，同时给出时序、资源和功耗报告。智能体利用仿真、综合和PPA反馈进行多轮迭代，修正功能并优化设计。其创新点在于把抽象层次作为核心变量，评估HLS对LLM智能体设计能力的影响，并构建可迭代的代理框架，使LLM从底层时序细节中解放出来，更专注于算法、并行度和架构权衡。

对比实验通常考察功能正确率、综合成功率、迭代次数、代码复杂度以及最终PPA（性能、功耗、面积）。论文结果表明，HLS抽象能降低LLM生成代码的难度，使其借助HLS工具的自动化优化获得更好的设计效率和正确性，尤其适合较复杂或算法密集型设计；但HLS也引入工具约束、pragma调优和验证复杂性，最终质量仍取决于高层描述和综合指令。因此，更高抽象并非简单替代RTL，而是改变智能体的设计空间和优化目标。

该研究对ASIC/FPGA加速器、边缘AI芯片、领域专用架构和快速原型设计具有启发意义：未来LLM芯片设计可能采用多层代理流程，高层代理负责算法与架构，底层代理负责RTL与物理实现，并与HLS、逻辑综合和验证工具闭环。其影响在于推动芯片设计自动化和设计空间探索，但验证可信度、PPA可预测性和工具兼容性仍是待解决问题。UCLA的工作表明，HLS可能是释放LLM智能体芯片设计能力的重要方向。
